decisions.rationale: Gastroenterology is the canonical home for gastric-cancer alarm-feature recognition and endoscopic investigation; the GS competency is substantially the same.

deferred_groups.rationale: The zero-coverage Psychiatry unit bundles ASD and ADHD, which map to separate pediatric owners (SU-P-046 and SU-P-047); one PRIMARY_OWNER cannot represent both safely without splitting the established unit.

MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: the unit bundles Kayser-Fleischer/Wilson-disease recognition and young-patient arcus/dyslipidemia screening, which have different natural external owners; one PRIMARY_OWNER would distort the established unit.

MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: this unit bundles optic/retinal RAPD interpretation, compressive third-nerve-palsy emergency recognition, and pharmacologic pupil abnormalities; one owner would not safely represent the established multi-competency unit.
MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: this unit bundles distinct reporting triggers (child protection, police, coroner/registrar, long-term-care, driving, and flying) with no single safe external owner.
MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: the unit bundles pulmonary cystic-fibrosis recognition with multisystem complications whose natural counterparts differ; one owner would distort the established unit.
MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: PCOS, menstrual disorders, and menopause have separate Gynecology counterparts; no single external owner safely represents the combined Endocrinology cross-reference.
MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: the pure cross-reference combines wounds/ulcers and pediatric exanthems, whose canonical counterparts are in different chapters.
MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: the Pediatrics source heading resolves to separate NF1 and NF2 study units, so no single canonical owner safely represents the Neurology cross-reference.

MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: the cross-reference bundles endocrine paraneoplastic syndromes and CNS tumours, whose canonical counterparts differ; no single external owner safely represents the established unit.

MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: Gastroenterology combines diagnosis with gluten-free-diet management across chronic diarrhea, malabsorption, and abnormal liver tests, while Pediatrics focuses on pediatric diarrhea and failure-to-thrive presentation; no single owner safely represents the bundled competencies.

PRIOR_OWNERSHIP_INTERACTION_CONFLICT: the canonical SU-E-48 PRIMARY_OWNER / SU-FM-46 CROSS_LINK pair substantially shares osteoporosis, while SU-E-51 tests distinct Paget disease; the current group schema cannot preserve that pair and represent the mixed distinct relationship without contradiction.

MULTI_COMPETENCY_OWNER_CONFLICT: the units share epistaxis bleeding-management coverage, but SU-OT-33 also bundles facial-trauma and specialist recognition competencies; unit-level roles cannot isolate the shared subset safely, strengthening the recommendation for a future competency-level ownership layer.

MIXED_RELATIONSHIP_SCHEMA_LIMITATION: Cardiology and Infectious Diseases overlap in general infective-endocarditis recognition and prophylaxis but retain chapter-specific diagnostic framing, while Pediatrics independently tests congenital-heart-disease risk and pediatric prophylaxis; whole-unit links would suppress legitimate competency coverage and mixed shared/distinct roles cannot be represented safely.
